contexts.text: This is what glorification signifies in .
Nothing is sweeter to him than to worship the Lord, and to glorify (praise) Him every day.

In proportion as He put off this (infirm human), and put on the Divine Human, He was in another state, which state is called the state of His glorification... In this state of glorification He spoke to Jehovah as to Himself; for He was Jehovah Himself. AC 1999:end. AC 2265.
Thus did He continually ascend to glorification, that is, to union, which is what is said in .
By glorification is meant union.

That the Lord had two states... one of humiliation, the other of glorification. References. Therefore there were also two states of perception; He was in the state of glorification, that is, of union of the Human with the Divine, when He perceived these things which are contained in the internal sense of this chapter.
To be circumcised, when predicated of the Lord, = to be glorified, thus to put off the human, and put on the Divine. To be glorified means to put on the Divine.
I heard a general glorification of the Lord. Described. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

This glorification takes place when the Angels are in a state of tranquility and peace; for it then flows forth from their inmost joys... [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
When He put off this human, He put on the Divine Human... The former state was that of the Lord's humiliation; but the latter of His glorification.
But in the state of glorification, when the Human essence has become united to the Divine one... He then does not intercede, but has mercy... renders aid, and saves.
The Lord had two states... His state of glorification was when He was in the Divine which He had from Jehovah His Father...
The passover represented the Lord's glorification, and thus the conjunction of the Divine with the human race.
That the Lord successively made His Rational Divine, and continually purified it, is evident from, I have glorified it, and will glorify it again.
To glorify = to make Divine.
It treats (in ) of the unition of the Human essence with the Divine essence, or glorification, through temptations.
The passion of the cross was the last of the Lord's temptation, by which He fully united the Human to the Divine, and the Divine to the Human, and thus glorified Himself.
Unless the Lord had assumed the Human, and glorified it.
As it was Divine love from which the Lord... sanctified and glorified Himself...
Until He had glorified (the Divine Rational).
Now I know that thou fearest God = glorification from Divine love; (for) to know, when predicated of the Lord's Divine, = to be united, or, what is the same, to be glorified.
The Lord not only regenerated, but also glorified Himself, that is, made Himself Divine.

Hence... the regeneration of man is an image of the glorification of the Lord: or, what is the same, in the process of man's regeneration, there may be seen, as in an image, although remotely, the process of the Lord's glorification. AC 3141. AC 3296:end.
But with the Lord there was not regeneration, but glorification; that is, all things in both the Rational and the Natural were by Him made Divine.
In man's regeneration, which is an image of the Lord's glorification, the case is this. AC 4027. AC 4237:end. AC 4538:3.

A new state. Signified... A new state is a state of glorification of the Rational, as before in respect to good, so now in respect to truth. The Rational was glorified when it was made Divine as to both.
That the Lord as to the Human was made new, that is, glorified, or, what is the same, was made Divine, can never be apprehended... by one who is in worldly and corporeal loves...
The state of the Lord's glorification may in some measure be apprehended from the state of the regeneration of man... AC 3212:4, Explained.

The Lord completely cast out all the evil which was hereditary with Him from the mother, and made Himself Divine even as to the vessels, that is, as to the truths. This is what, in the Word, is called glorification.
Jehovah was in Him; thus, so long as the Human was not glorified, the appearing of Jehovah was Divine perception...

It treats, in the supreme sense, of how the Lord made His Human Divine; and in the representative sense, of how the Lord regenerates man, that is, makes him celestial and spiritual: that the regeneration of man is an image of the Lord's glorification. References.
It treats here... in the supreme sense, of the glorification of the Lord's Natural; and in the representative sense, of the regeneration of the Natural with man.

That the Lord, from the Divine good of the Divine Rational... willed, through the good of the Natural... to acquire truth by means of which He might glorify or make Divine His Natural; or that the Lord, from the Divine truth of the Divine Rational... willed, through the truth of the Natural... to acquire truth, by means of which He might glorify or make Divine His Rational. Explained.
It treats here... in the supreme sense, of the glorification of the Natural in the Lord, that is, of how the Lord made the Natural in Himself Divine... AC 3656.
Man says that he himself is justified... but does not think that the Lord was glorified...
Before He was glorified. He was the Divine truth which is from Divine good; but when He was glorified. He was Divine good itself as to both essences... AC 4577.
The passover = the Lord's glorification, that is, the putting on of the Divine as to the Human...
Thus He reduced into order both Heaven and Hell, and this successively, even until He had fully glorified Himself. AC 4287:2.
As regeneration can fall into man's idea, but not so well the Lord's glorification...
It treats of the glorification of the Lord as to the Divine Natural. AC 4585:4. AC 5346:end. AC 5398:end.
For the Lord glorified Himself, that is, made Himself Divine, according to Divine order. AC 4538:3.
For the Lord's glorification proceeded from truth to the good of truth, and finally to good.
When the Lord glorified Himself, He made His Human the Divine esse or Jehovah (References.); but previous to this. He made His Human holy; such was the process of the Lord's glorification.
The Lord's glorification proceeded from external things to interior ones...
This Divine good into which the Lord was born is here treated of. Its derivations are what came forth into the Lord's Human... and by these He glorified it.
The Lord expelled this infirm human... and made the Human in Himself Divine, which is meant by His being glorified.
He could have no other Human when it was glorified.
The Lord's Human, after it was glorified or made Divine, cannot be conceived of as human, but as Divine love in a human form...
The Divine truth... which, after He was glorified, went forth from Him.
The Internal of the Lord, which was Human, was the Celestial of the Spiritual from the Rational; of this and of its glorification it treats where Joseph is treated of. AC 5005.
When He was glorified, that is, when He made the Human in Himself Divine, He then became Divine good, from which the Divine truth then proceeded.

In the preceding chapter it treated of the Lord, how He glorified or made Divine the interior things of His Natural; here, therefore, it treats of how He glorified or made Divine the exterior things of His Natural... which are properly called the corporeal things, or the sensuous things of both kinds together with the recipients; for the latter together with the former constitute that which is called the body. The Lord made the very Corporeal in Himself Divine, both its sensuous things and their recipients, and therefore He rose from the sepulchre with the body...
The Lord alone rose (with the body with which He was encompassed in the world); and this because He glorified or made Divine His body, while He was in the world.

This of Jehovah in Heaven is the Lord from eternity: the Lord took on Him the same when He glorified or made the Human in Himself Divine; which is also manifestly evident from the form in which He appeared... when He was transfigured... and in which He sometimes appeared to the prophets...
The Lord's glorification is described by the vine and its shoots ().
(The Angels discourse about) such things as are contained in the internal sense... namely, about the Lord's glorification...

When He was glorified. He had (foresight and Providence) from the Divine alone; for the Human glorified is Divine. Regarded in itself, the human is nothing but a form recipient of life from the Divine: but the Lord's Human glorified, or His Divine Human, is not a form recipient of life from the Divine, but is the very esse of life...

By the seven years of plenty, and by the seven years of famine... are described... in the supreme sense the states of the glorification of the Lord's Human... By Pharaoh is meant the Natural, the glorification of which in the Lord is there treated of. The things which took place at that time... were representative of... the glorification of His Human...

What Joseph represents is called the Celestial of the Spiritual from the Natural... thus it is the truth of good from His Divine Human; this the Lord was while He lived in the world; but when He glorified Himself, He mounted above it, and became Divine good itself... even as to the Human.

Therefore the Divine things in the internal sense... concerning the... glorification of His Human, affect (the Angels) to such a degree that they perceive from it all the blessedness of their wisdom and intelligence.

All things related concerning Joseph and his brethren, in the supreme sense, represent the glorification of the Lord's Human; that is, how the Lord made the Human in Himself Divine. (Why this is represented.)

Moreover, the glorification of the Lord's Human is the pattern of the regeneration of man; therefore the regeneration of man is presented in the internal sense... where the Lord's glorification is presented. AC 7166:end.
What is successive and continuous of the Lord's glorification. Treated of.
The Lord's body itself, when glorified, that is, made Divine, is nothing (but Divine love).
When He was in the world He made His Human to be Divine truth; but afterwards, when He was fully glorified, He made it to be Divine good, thus one with Jehovah. Treated of.

In the inmost sense of the whole Word, it treats solely of the Lord, and of the glorification of His Human; but as this sense transcends the human understanding, we may explain the Word as to its internal sense, in which it treats of... regeneration... because the regeneration of man is an image representative of the Lord's glorification. References.
Afterwards, He completely glorified His Human, and made it Divine good. Explained.
These were the degrees of the Lord's glorification, which are here described in the internal sense.
By temptations... at the same time to glorify His Human, that is, to make it Divine.
Because the regeneration of man, which is effected by means of temptations, is an image of the glorification of the Lord. References.

But after the Lord had fully glorified Himself, which was done when He had endured the last of temptation on the cross, He made His Human also Divine good... Hence it is evident what is meant by... The Holy Spirit was not yet, because Jesus was not yet glorified (). AC 8573.
In the supreme sense, by the passover is represented the damnation of the unfaithful, and the deliverance of the faithful by the Lord, when He was glorified.

The Spiritual Church, who could not have been saved, unless the Lord had... glorified His Human, that is, made it Divine... Therefore, in the supreme sense, by these words is signified that the glorification and resurrection of the Lord as to His Human is the source of all salvation.
As the glorification of the Lord... was signified by the eatings... For the glorification of the Lord... proceeds from the affection of truth.
This glorification by choirs lasted about an hour... [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

I will be Glorified () = that they would see a Divine effect from the Lord's Divine Human in the dissipation of falsity... To be Glorified, when said of the Lord, = a Divine effect; here, from His Divine Human; because by coming into the world, and assuming the Human and making it Divine, the Lord cast all evils and falsities into the Hells, and reduced the Heavens into order, and also delivered from damnation those of the spiritual Church... These things in general are signified by to be Glorified.
As to Glorification upon Pharaoh... AC 8137:3. AC 8188. AC 8190. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

In the internal sense of this chapter, the Lord is celebrated, in that after He had glorified His Human, He cast down into the Hells the evil who were infesting the good, and elevated into Heaven the good who had been infested.
Then sang Moses... = the glorification of the Lord by those of the Spiritual Church, for deliverance. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.] AC 8263.
The reason why to sing a song = to glorify (praise)...
Hence by them is signified the glorification of the Lord, that is, the celebration of Him from gladness of heart. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
The Angels with the men were at the same time in glorification of the Lord... [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
Because the glorification of the Lord in the Heavens is effected by means of choirs. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

Hence it is that the glorifications of the Lord with the ancients... were effected by means of songs, psalms, musical instruments... [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
That prophetic songs in the internal sense contained the glorification of the Lord. Illustrated. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
From these passages it is evident, that a song is a glorification of the Lord for deliverance. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
Gladness of heart, together with the exaltation of the Lord, is what is meant by Glorification. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

The Lord does not want glory for His own sake, but for the sake of the man who Glorifies Him. The man who Glorifies Him does it from a holy reverence for Him... and from humiliation of himself... and as in such glorification of the Lord there is thus holy reverence and humiliation, he is in a state to receive the influx of good from the Lord, thus also love to Him. Hence it is that the Lord wills glorification by man. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
Then Miriam... took a timbrel... = the glorification of the Lord from the good of faith. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

The Lord... before He was fully glorified, was Divine truth, and therefore at that time there was mediation... But after He was glorified as to the Human, He was called the Mediator... from this. Explained.
But when He was glorified. He became Divine good even as to the Human... Illustrated.
If they are told... that to the likeness of (the Divine love) He glorified His Human...
In the inmost or supreme sense it treats... especially of the glorification of His Human...
To be glorified in God () = to become Divine good from which is Divine truth.
The veil of the temple rent in twain... = the Lord's glorification...
The glorification of the Human even to the Divine good... is described... by the process of expiation... AC 9670:5. AC 9670:6.

By continual combats with the Hells the Lord glorified His Human, that is, made it Divine; for as man is regenerated by means of combats... so the Lord by means of combats... was glorified. Hence the glorification of the Lord's Human from His Own power is merit and justice; for thereby man is saved...

The Holy Spirit was not yet, because Jesus was not yet glorified (means) that while the Lord was in the world. He Himself taught Divine truth; but when He was glorified, which was after His resurrection. He taught it through Angels and Spirits.
It treats (in ) of the glorification of the Lord as to the Human, which is signified by the inauguration of Aaron and his sons into the priesthood.
As the regeneration of man is an image of the Lord's glorification, it is evident that the Lord glorified Himself in this Way.
As the glorification of the Lord as to His Human transcends the human understanding... it is explained by its image.
The reason why the sacrifices and burnt-offerings, in the supreme sense, = the glorification of the Lord's Human... AC 10047:3.
To glorify the Human is to make it Divine. AC 10052:2. AC 10828:end.

As to the glorification of the Lord's Human, it was effected by means of the unition of Divine truth with Divine good. Explained... He made His Human Divine truth through Divine means, especially through combats... and in proportion as He united it. He glorified it, that is, made it Divine. Signified.
That the Lord... made His Human Divine truth, and united it with the Divine good which was in Himself, and thus glorified His Human. References.

As the Lord glorified His Human, so also He regenerates man. Explained... He flows in with good through the soul... and with truth through the hearing and sight... and in proportion as a man desists from evils, the Lord conjoins good with truth...
It cannot be said of His Human that it was regenerated, but that it was glorified; for His Inmost... was the Divine Itself...
The glorification of His internal man, or of His internal Human, is described by representatives in the burnt-offerings from rams and lambs.
This is a burnt-offering to Jehovah = the glorification of the Lord's Human.
The burnt-offerings signified the unition of Divine truth with Divine good, which unition is what is meant by glorification...

That glorification, where the Lord is treated of, is the unition of His Human with the Divine Itself which was in Him... by which unition He made His Human also Divine good, is evident from the passages in the Word where glory and glorification are mentioned in relation to the Lord. Illustrated.

Hence it is evident that the unition of the Lord as to the Human with the Divine Itself which was in Him... is glorification; for it is said that God will glorify Him in Himself (). It is also evident that this unition was fully effected by the passion of the cross...
That when the Lord was glorified the Divine truth proceeded from Him. Illustrated.
Thus the glorification or unition was reciprocal, as the Lord teaches in .

From this some idea may be apprehended concerning the glorification of the Lord's Human; for as the Lord glorified His Human, so He regenerates man; and therefore... the regeneration of man is an image of the Lord's glorification. From this it is evident that the first state of His glorification was to make His Human Divine truth, and to unite it with the Divine good which was in Him; and that the second state was to act from Divine good through Divine truth... These are the things which are described by the sacrifices and burnt-offerings... treated of in . AC 10060. Explained. AC 10076, Explained.

Therefore the Lord's glorification as to His Human is representatively described in the process of the inauguration of Aaron and his sons; the first state of glorification by those things which are said concerning the sacrifice from the bullock and the burnt-offering from the first ram; and the second state of glorification, by those things which are said concerning the second ram, which is called the ram of fillings. The first state is called anointing, and the second state, the filling of the hand...

Thou shalt do thus to Aaron and his sons = this representative of the glorification of the Lord... To do thus, that is, to anoint them and fill their hands, and thus inaugurate them into the priesthood, = to represent the Lord as to the glorification of His Human, and the influx thence into the Heavens and the Church; for the anointing was a representative of the glorification of His Human; and the filling of the hands, of His influx thence into the Heavens and the Church.
Glorification... is the unition of the Divine Human with the Divine Itself... [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

Therefore, His Human, after glorification, was not like the human in a man. On this account, the Lord took into Heaven all His glorified Human... and left nothing of it in the sepulchre... That the Lord glorified His very body, even to its ultimates, which are the bones and the flesh. Illustrated.

The baptism of the Lord Himself = the glorification of His Human... for that in the Word which = the regeneration of man, also = the glorification of the Human in the Lord; for the regeneration of man is an image of the Lord's glorification.
To fulfil all the righteousness of God = to subjugate the Hells... and at the same time to glorify His Human; which things were effected by temptations... AC 10239:end.
By (the glorification of His Human) He put Himself in power...

As to (the feast of unleavened things) it properly = the glorification of the Lord's Human; thus the remembrance of it, and thanksgiving on account of it; for by it... man has deliverance from evils, and salvation. For the Lord glorified His Human by combats against the Hells, and victories: the last combat and victory was on the cross; and therefore He then fully glorified Himself. Illustrated.
To glorify the Son of Man () = to make the Human Divine. This is evidently said of the passion of the cross.
From this it is evident that by the passion of the cross, the Lord not only subjugated the Hells, but also plenarily glorified His Human...
Because by the subjugation of the Hells by the Lord, and by the glorification of His Human, comes all deliverance from evil... AC 10659.
The Lord came... also that He might glorify His Human, in order that by it He might keep all things in order to eternity...
Six days thou shalt do work = the first state of regeneration... and in the supreme sense, of the glorification of the Lord's Human. Explained.

The Sabbath... = the second state of regeneration... and in the supreme sense, the union of the Lord's Human with the Divine Itself... for when He went out of the world. He made His Human Divine good by union with the Divine Itself which was in Him... The Lord does the like with the man whom He regenerates... and this is represented by the Sabbath in the relative sense; for the regeneration of man is an image of the Lord's glorification; that is, as the Lord glorified His Human, so He regenerates man.
As there was such a union... in the Lord, He rose not only as to the soul, but also as to the body which He had glorified in the world. Signified.

The Lord saved the human race by this, that He subjugated the Hells... and at the same time by this, that He glorified His Human; for thus He can keep the Hells subjugated to eternity. The subjugation of the Hells, and the simultaneous glorification of His Human, was effected by means of temptations...
That He glorified His Human; and that the passion of the cross was the last temptation and full victory, by which He was glorified. Illustrated.
The reason the Lord rose not only as to the spirit, but also as to the body, is that He glorified, that is, made Divine, all His Human, when He was in the world.
That the Lord glorified His Human in the world. (References to passages on this subject.)
That the glorification of the Lord's Human... was effected by means of temptations. (References, to passages.)
3. That the Lord came into the world to glorify the Human, that is, to unite it to the Divine which was in Him from conception. DLord 12, General article.
That the passion of the cross was the last combat... by which He... fully glorified His Human.
General article.
Glorification is the unition of the Divine and the Human; and therefore it is said, and God shall glorify Him in Himself.
That He rose again on the third day = glorification.
After... He had glorified His Human, that is, united it to the Divine of His Father.

In the world the Lord had two states, which are called the state of humiliation... and the state of glorification, or of unition with the Divine which is called the Father; the state of humiliation in proportion as and when He was in the human from the mother, and the state of glorification in proportion as and when He was in the Human from the Father. In the state of humiliation He prayed to the Father... in the state of glorification He spoke to the Father as to Himself. In this state He said that the Father was in Him, and He in the Father, and that the Father and He were one; but in the state of humiliation He underwent temptations...
From these passages it is evident, that the Lord as to the glorified Human was not the son of Mary or of David.
The quality of His glorified Human, He showed... when He was transfigured.
That the Lord's Human was glorified. Illustrated.
As the Lord's Human was glorified, that is, made Divine, therefore after death He rose on the third day with the whole body. Illustrated.
For after the glorification or plenary unition with the Father, which was effected by the passion of the cross, the Lord was the Divine wisdom and the Divine truth itself, thus the Holy Spirit.
The glorification of the Lord is the glorification of His Human which He assumed in the world; and the glorified Human of the Lord is the Divine Natural.
The Christian faith in a universal idea is. That the Lord... came... to subjugate the Hells, and glorify His Human; and that without this no mortal man could be saved. AR 67. BE 116. TCR 2.

It is also a universal of faith, that He came... in order that He might glorify the Human which He took in the world, that is, might unite it to the Divine a quo; and might thus keep Hell... in obedience to eternity. AR 67:2. BE 116:2. TCR 2:2.
As He fully glorified the natural Human even to its ultimates. He therefore rose again with the whole body...
This is meant by the two states... of exinanition, and of glorification.

When He went out of the world, He fully united Divine truth to the Divine good which was in Him from conception; for the Lord glorified, that is, made Divine, His Human, as He makes man spiritual. (Explained.)

Now follows a glorification of the Lord on that account... The glorification of the Lord which now follows, is first made by the higher Heavens, afterwards by the lower Heavens, and finally by the lowest Heavens. Illustrated. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.] AE 321.

They sang a new song = the acknowledgement and glorification of the Lord, that He alone is Judge, Redeemer, and Saviour, thus the God of Heaven and earth. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

The reason a song also = glorification, which is confession from joy of heart, is that singing exalts and causes the affection to break forth from the heart into sound, and present itself intensely in its life. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
The confession and glorification of the Lord by the Angels of the lower Heavens. Signified. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.] AE 335.
The confession and glorification of the Lord by the Angels of the lowest Heavens. Signified. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.] AE 342.
When man is thinking... of the Lord's passion, the Angels perceive His glorification, and at the same time His resurrection. TCR 706:4.

A confession and glorification by the Angels of Heaven, that the Lord is He who is, who lives and has power from Himself, and rules all things, because He alone is eternal and infinite. Signified. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
To give thanks = acknowledgement and glorification of the Lord. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
A celebration and glorification of the Lord before Him, and before the Angels of the higher Heavens. Signified. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
As it were a new song = the celebration and glorification of the Lord in the New Christian Heaven... [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.] AR 618.
Who shall not... glorify Thy name () = that He alone is to be worshipped... To glorify His name = to worship Him. AE 942. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

In proportion as she has Glorified herself () = in the degree according to their elation of heart from dominion; for from this they glorify (praise) themselves. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

Preface. A glorification of the Lord by the Angels... that the Roman Catholic religiosity in the Spiritual World is removed. Signified. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]
Let us be glad and exult, and give glory to Him = joy of soul and of heart, and the derivative glorification of the Lord... [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

To give glory to Him = to acknowledge, and confess that all truth is from the Lord; also to acknowledge that the Lord is the God of Heaven and earth; here, therefore, it = to glorify (praise) Him, because this involves both of these things.
He uttered these words after His glorification, and His glorification was His full unition with His Father... and the Holy Spirit was the Divine proceeding from Him after His glorification.
(The notion that the joy of Heaven consists in the perpetual glorification of God.) [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.] CL 9. TCR 695.

By the glorification of God is meant to bring forth the fruits of love, that is, to do the work of our calling faithfully, sincerely, and with diligence... By this is God Glorified, and in this case by worship at stated times. Have you never read... In this is My Father Glorified, that ye bring forth much fruit... (). You priests can be in the glorification of worship, because this is your office... [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.]

From the east to the west... was heard a glorification; and the Angel said to me, This glorification is a glorification of the Lord on account of His Advent... The glorifications and celebrations of the Lord are made from the Word. Illustrated. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.] CL 81:3.

There was (then) heard a general glorification from the east into the west of Heaven, and also from the south into the north. Illustrated. [Here, glorification is being used in the sense of its meaning praise.] TCR 625.
The passion... was not the act of redemption, but the act of the glorification of His Human.
This union is glorification.

That the state of progression to union was His state of exinanition, and the union itself is the state of His glorification. The Lord... had two states, which are called those of exinanition and of glorification... The state of glorification is also the state of union; He was in this state when He was transfigured... and also when He did miracles...
The reason He had these two states, of exinanition and of glorification. Explained.
In a Word, the Lord glorified His Human, that is, made it Divine, in the same way as He regenerates man, that is, makes him spiritual. TCR 684:end.
He asked the Father to glorify His name, that is, His Human. To glorify is to make Divine by union with Himself.
Who divide the spoil, and then are glad and glorify (praise).
That the passion... was the last temptation... and was the means of the glorification of His Human, that is, of union with the Divine of His Father; and was not redemption. General article.
The glorification is the unition of the Lord with the Divine of His Father; this was done successively, and plenarily by the passion...

Concerning the glorification, by which is meant the unition of the Lord's Divine Human with the Divine of the Father, and that it was fully completed by the passion... Illustrated. AE 806:6. CanonsNC 20. Redeemer. 7. 5.
The Divine and the Human, after the glorification, being united as the prior with its posterior, and as the essence with its form.
The Lord... by combats... glorified His Human, that is, made it Divine; so with man... after temptation. He glorifies him, that is, renders him spiritual.
On a general glorification in the Heavens. SE 604. a. SE 606. SE 3029. SE 4176.
Some in Hell wanted to glorify (praise) too.
(The glorification of the Lord's body.) Explained.
To glorify (praise) the Lord is not use, but recreation; for they glorify (praise) the Lord in every use...
Thus and no otherwise is the Lord Glorified in man... In this is My Father Glorified...
As the Lord when He glorified His Human (Signified); namely, that He dissipated all evils and falsities from the human He had from the mother.

As He glorified His Human, so He regenerates man; that is, as He united His Divine to the Human and the Human to the Divine, so, with man, he conjoins the internal with the external and the external with the internal.
Because the Divine truth proceeds from the Lord's glorified Human, and not immediately from His Divine Itself, because this was glorified in Him from eternity. Signified.
To glorify () = to make Divine.
